who: Historian of medicine at Western University, PhD Toronto 1999.

evidence.says: Western identifies McKellar as a history professor with a Toronto PhD (1999), and lists Medicine and Technology in Canada, 1900-1950 among her books.
The examination certificate for Shauna Devine's Producing Knowledge dissertation names Dr. Shelley McKellar as supervisor at Western Ontario.
The authority cites Shelley McKellar on Medicine and Technology in Canada, 1900-1950 (2008) and The Career of Gordon Murray (1999).

notes: The authority's medical-history publications identify the Western professor; university, doctorate and student supervision agree.

who: Historian of modern German politics at Brooklyn College and the CUNY Graduate Center, DPhil Oxford.

evidence.says: CUNY's Winter 1998 newsletter identifies Christoph M. Kimmich as an Oxford DPhil, teaching at Brooklyn College since 1973 and the graduate school since 1975, specializing in twentieth-century German political history.
The authority for Christoph M. Kimmich cites German Foreign Policy, 1918-1945 (1981), whose title page identifies him with Brooklyn College, City University of New York.
Christian Kimmich is credited on Enhancing Energy Efficiency in Irrigation (2015), with the Swiss Federal Institute for Forest-Snow and Landscape Research.

notes: Christoph M. Kimmich matches the Oxford doctorate, CUNY appointment during 1985, and German-history field. Christian Kimmich is a different candidate.

who: American labor and public historian at North Carolina State University, PhD American Studies, Yale 1986.

evidence.says: NC State identifies David A. Zonderman as a history professor, lists a Yale American Studies PhD (1986), and credits Aspirations and Anxieties to him.
Lechner's university-posted CV records his NC State public-history doctorate in 2020 and names Dr. David A. Zonderman as chair.
The David A. Zonderman authority cites Aspirations and Anxieties (1992) and includes the variant name David Zonderman.

notes: Matching publication connects the authority to the professor; doctorate and student record also agree.

who: Historian of Canadian history and women's studies at Toronto, PhD London; author of Many Tender Ties.

evidence.says: The publisher identifies Sylvia Van Kirk as a Toronto professor of Canadian history and women's studies with a University of London PhD, and lists Many Tender Ties.
The Sylvia E. Kirk authority cites only the title-page name on The Dear Deceit (1993); it supplies no Toronto appointment or London doctorate.
S. Kirk is expanded as Stuart Kirk, affiliated with the Environment Agency's National Groundwater and Contaminated Land Centre and credited on groundwater publications.

notes: Stuart Kirk is a different person. No evidence connects Sylvia E. Kirk to Sylvia Van Kirk; the sparse authority does not conclusively establish whether they are different people.

who: Charles Hallan McCarthy, American history professor and Knights of Columbus chair at Catholic University of America.

evidence.says: Catholic University's department history identifies Charles Hallan McCarthy as its first Knights of Columbus Chair of American History, with approximately 35 years of service before retirement in the late 1930s.
The university identifies Charles McCarthy as the professor teaching American constitutional history and United States history before his retirement.
The authority expands Charles H. McCarthy as Charles Hallan McCarthy and cites Lincoln's Plan of Reconstruction, noting graduate study at the University of Pennsylvania.
Columbia's library catalogue attributes Lincoln's Plan of Reconstruction to Charles H. (Charles Hallan) McCarthy and records its original publication in 1901.

notes: The full-name candidate matches Catholic University's American historian during 1915. The other candidates do not provide a competing institutional match.

who: Leonid Ivanovich Strakhovsky, historian of Russia and Europe, professor at Maryland in 1937-1942 and later Toronto.

evidence.says: The scholarly biographical article identifies Leonid Ivanovich Strakhovsky as a history doctorate of Louvain and professor of European history at Maryland in 1937-1942, later teaching at Harvard and Toronto.
The authority for Leonid Ivan Strakhovsky includes the fuller form Leonid Ivanovich Strakhovskii and cites L'empereur Nicolas I (1928).
The University of Toronto Press book's author biography identifies Leonid I. Strakhovsky as a Louvain history doctorate and former faculty member at Maryland, Georgetown and Harvard.

notes: The authority's expanded name and Russian-history work identify the historian whose Maryland appointment covers Metcalf's 1942 doctorate.

who: Architectural historian at the University of Texas at Austin from 1987, PhD Art History and Archaeology, Columbia.

evidence.says: UT identifies Alofsin as an architectural historian and Frank Lloyd Wright specialist, director of its architecture center in 1990-1993, and holder of a Columbia doctorate.
The university archive's biography records Alofsin joining UT Austin's School of Architecture in 1987 and subsequently founding its architecture PhD program.
The Anthony Alofsin authority cites architectural publications, including Socorro and Frank Lloyd Wright (1999).
UT records Christopher Long's doctorate there in 1993 and identifies his dissertation as a study of architect Josef Frank.

notes: The name, architectural publications, UT appointment and relevant period agree with the AHA supervisor record.

who: AHA-listed Kansas State history supervisor of David Edwards's 1967 dissertation; fuller identity not independently established.

evidence.says: The publisher preview of The Parish Clergy in Nineteenth-Century Russia cites D. W. Edwards's Kansas State dissertation, Orthodoxy during the Reign of Nicholas I (1967), but does not identify its supervisor.
Robert L. (Robert Lane) Bowden is identified as an extension plant pathologist on Wheat Foliar Fungicides (1992).
Kansas State lists Robert L. Bowden as an adjunct professor of plant pathology appointed in 1989, with a Wisconsin-Madison PhD in 1989.
Robert J. Bowden is affiliated with the US Environmental Protection Agency's Great Lakes National Program Office on a Lake Michigan survey.
Robert L. Bowden is credited with designing Pittsburgh walking and museum maps; the authority gives no academic career facts.

notes: Reviewed all eleven candidate authorities. Several identify unrelated fields or incompatible careers; the sparse remaining records cannot all be conclusively excluded. No source found connects a candidate to history supervision at Kansas State in 1967.
